title: Bank Deposit Shortfall Delivery Amount and Make-Good Delivery Rate
content:
On a Bank Deposit shortfall delivery, the amount delivered is the make-good held converted at the make-good delivery rate.

## Definitions

**Make-good held.** The make-good held is the principal Paloma holds on the transfer: the principal collected plus Paloma's credits, less the payouts sent and the principal refunds issued, each a total of the matching entries on the transfer's ledger in US dollars.

**Booking-day reference.** The transfer's locked exchange rate divided by one minus the tier's exchange-rate margin over one hundred.

**Make-good delivery rate.** The booking-day reference multiplied by one hundred less the delivery margin plus the wallet rate bonus and the tenure rate bonus, all in percentage points, over one hundred; then raised by the delay uplift as a percentage of that result (multiplied by one hundred plus the delay uplift, over one hundred); rounded half up to four decimals.

**Values used.** The delivery margin is the tier's exchange-rate margin; the wallet rate bonus and the tenure rate bonus are 0 percentage points, and the delay uplift is 0 percent.

**Amount delivered.** The make-good held multiplied by the make-good delivery rate, rounded half up to two decimals of the payout currency once at the end.

## Worked example (hypothetical transfer whose tier exchange-rate margin is taken as 0.95 percent)

Ledger: principal collected 500.00; Paloma's credits 25.22; payouts sent 500.00; principal refunds issued 0.00. Locked exchange rate 18.3243.

| Step | Working | Figure |
|---|---|---|
| Make-good held | 500.00 plus 25.22, less 500.00, less 0.00 | 25.22 US dollars |
| Booking-day reference | 18.3243 divided by one minus 0.95 over one hundred | 18.500050... |
| Before the uplift | 18.500050... multiplied by one hundred less 0.95 plus 0 plus 0, over one hundred | 18.3243 |
| Raised by the delay uplift | multiplied by one hundred plus 0, over one hundred | 18.3243 |
| Make-good delivery rate | rounded half up to four decimals | 18.3243 |
| Amount delivered | 25.22 multiplied by 18.3243, rounded half up to two decimals | 462.14 pesos |

## Basis questions

**Is the booking-day reference rounded on its own?** No. Only the make-good delivery rate is rounded, to four decimals, and the amount delivered, to two decimals at the end.

**Which margin enters the booking-day reference?** The tier's exchange-rate margin, from the transfer's tier.
